title: Surviving the bugaloo era
summary: Back in New York the band played Casa Blanca and Chez Jose; Machito says a solid professional organization still worked three or four times a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: When you came back, did you get work right away?
No, but in a month or so we was organizing. We was playing at the Casa Blanca, the Chez Jose, and, you know, ....
Yeah, the Chez Jose was popular at the time.
Now the bugaloo was reaching its peak then. First the pachanga hurt you, now you come back from Puerto Rico, the bugaloo is there, did that hurt you?
Okay. They were hiring the young kids' bands .... Right?
How did the band survive then?

Well, I always believe that something with quality always prevail. Ahh - you have a solid organization and people always respect the organization that is solid, that it give a good service; because we was a mature band. Not just because the people was an advanced age or whatever, is that we had the responsibility of a professional organization. We wasn't like young kids celebrating to play a dance because they are going to meet a lot of girls and nothing like that. We were doing that because we made living out of it. So our responsibility was different.
Well, because of the popularity of bugaloo, were you able to work as often as you would have liked to?

Listen, I don't recall very well, but we were doing all right playing three or four times a week, practically what we were doing before. Sometimes we might have two dates, but we were doing, considering ...
